notes.title: Hotfix for Steam API
notes.notes: A small update to the recent patch, restoring Steam API functionality. If you missed an achievement, many of them will show up when you load your save or talk to a person. Others will require you to re-trigger them. We apologize for any inconvenience!

notes.title: Ossuary Updated to 1.8.2
notes.notes:
This update fixes an issue where the framerate would drop when moving diagonally.

Note that [url=https://futureproofgames.com/blog/2021/08/17/mac-support-ending-2022/]we no longer support Mac[/url], so we're afraid this update applies only to Windows.

notes.title: MacOS Support Ending in 2022
notes.notes: Starting January 1, 2022, we will no longer provide support for MacOS versions of our games. We won't be preventing access to Mac downloads, but we will no longer dedicate development time to supporting new OS versions, nor will we be issuing new updates. For more information, [url=https://futureproofgames.com/blog/2021/08/17/mac-support-ending-2022/]see our blog post and FAQ[/url].

notes.title: Maintenance Update - 64-bit Mac Support
notes.notes: We've updated [i]Ossuary[/i] and its demo, "The Hodge-Podge Transformer", to provide support for modern Mac OSes. Please let us know if you run into any issues!

notes.title: UX Improvements to Ossuary (v 1.8)
notes.notes:
We've released version 1.8 of Ossuary today! It includes the following improvements:[list]
    [*]Improved control explanations in the early area of the game.
    [*]Volume controls are now also available in the Options area.
    [*]The dev notebook is now navigable in fullscreen.
    [*]Floor markers now highlight with higher contrast colors and a sound effect. This should help colorblind players solve those puzzles.
[/list]

notes.title: Striking A Discord: Ossuary
notes.notes:
I choose to see the funny side of Ossuary, a gloriously strange Discordian adventure game from Future Proof, home of Gregory Avery-Weir, creator of (I Fell In Love With) The Majesty Of Colours and Looming. Upon its initial release back in 2013, I found Ossuary baffling. “What could it all mean?” I asked, never expecting anybody to answer. I played it eventually and while I never managed to answer that initial query, I found a hundred more deliciously clever questions.

If you’ve ever stared at a list of upcoming releases and wished for something extraordinary to shake things up, pay attention to Ossuary. It’s coming to Steam on May 27th and deserves a second helping of devotees.
